transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Ever since that near-crash on the plane, every small noise or movement makes me jump out of my skin. I can’t function in meetings because I’m constantly on edge waiting for something bad to happen.
How long ago did this near-crash on the plane happen, and how long have you been feeling this way?
The near-crash happened six days ago on a red-eye flight. I have been feeling like this continuously since that night, and it hasn't let up for a single day.
Are you experiencing any repeated, unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the near-crash during the day or while you sleep?

Yes, during the day, scenes from the flight just slam into my head out of nowhere—the oxygen masks dropping, the flight attendant hitting the ceiling, and people screaming. For a few seconds, I feel like I'm right back in that seat, sweating and gripping the armrests like we're about to die, even if I'm just trying to read emails at my desk. It is terrifying and happens constantly.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, conversations, places, or activities that remind you of that flight?

Yes, absolutely. I cut people off if they bring up travel, and I won't even open my airline app because seeing a picture of a plane makes me feel physically sick. I've also been dodging meetings in our top-floor conference room because being up that high feels too much like being back in the air.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, or have you experienced any disturbing nightmares about the flight?

I haven't really experienced nightmares about the flight, and sleep itself hasn't been the main issue I've noticed. Sometimes I lie awake in bed feeling completely disconnected from everything, but once I fall asleep, I don't think I'm having bad dreams.
Did these intense feelings of panic, being on edge, and the flashbacks start immediately—within minutes or hours of the near-crash—or did they take a few days to develop?
They started immediately. As soon as the plane landed and in the hours right after, I was already completely on edge. It has been going on continuously for the last six days without any break at all.
Have you felt emotionally numb, or does it ever feel like your surroundings are unreal, as if you are living in a dream?

Yes, I feel both. I feel completely numb inside, like when my wife shares good news about the kids and I just can't feel any joy or warmth at all. Other times, the world feels flat and unreal, like I’m watching myself from across the room and stuck in a bad movie instead of being back in my own body.
Have you ever gone through any other highly traumatic or life-threatening events in your past, and if so, did you experience similar symptoms after that?
No, I have never been through anything highly traumatic or life-threatening in my past. This is the very first time I have ever felt anything like this.
Have you had any difficulty remembering specific, important details about the near-crash itself, or do you remember the entire event clearly?

No, I don't have any trouble remembering it at all—in fact, it is the exact opposite. The entire event is painfully clear, and those details constantly flash back in my mind. I can vividly picture the oxygen masks dropping, the flight attendant being thrown against the ceiling, and the sound of everyone screaming.
Over the past day or two, have you noticed these symptoms starting to fade or become less intense, or do they remain just as severe as they were right after the incident?
No, they haven't faded at all. They remain just as severe and intense as they were the very first day. It has been completely unrelenting for the past six days without any relief.
